column1: fb54ef Defines how your exchange rate moves and the risk of a currency crisis.
184332 The gap between the official exchange rate and the one the market considers fair. If it grows, speculators bet against the currency.
c01db3 A large deviation increases the risk of a forced devaluation.
9c6af2 Financing the government by creating new money. In the short term it pays the bills; in the medium term it causes inflation and depreciation.
2c07d3 Boosts the treasury today and inflation tomorrow.
7d82c3 Restrictions on taking money out of the country or buying foreign currency (for example, Argentina's «cepo»). They stop capital flight, but scare away investment.
ca7ee6 They reduce pressure on your currency in exchange for less growth.
752281 Foreign currency, gold and other assets the central bank holds to pay for imports and foreign debt and to defend the currency. A healthy level covers at least 3 months of imports.
b29ed0 If you rule you can buy or sell foreign currency to intervene, accumulate gold and create strategic oil reserves. They protect against crises.
0e3b2d The currencies of every country and their price against the dollar.
cd9a3a Exchange rates and how they change.
8f3006 What you can actually buy with your money. If your salary rises 5% and prices 10%, you are poorer.
700bc4 Compares your money adjusted for inflation.

7f69e8 A market where shares (pieces of ownership of companies) are bought and sold. Over the long run, stock markets have returned 6–10% a year on average, with sharp drops along the way (2008, 2020).
ad8c2b 32 real exchanges with companies inspired by real ones. Quotes move every business day on results, news and the economy.
a72efb The world's exchanges and indices (S&P 500, IPC, Ibovespa, DAX, Nikkei...). An index sums up how the largest companies in a market are doing.
adefa4 Choose an exchange to see its companies and indices.
e01e21 The set of your investments. Diversifying (holding many companies and sectors) reduces risk without reducing expected return much.
acca51 Your positions, open profit, margin and shorts.
815e39 Instructions to buy or sell. Market order: executes right away at the current price. Limit: only at your price or better. Stop: triggers if the price crosses a level, to cut losses.
74a9e3 Pending orders that execute on their own when the price gets there.
e14604 Acquiring shares to profit if they rise (long position) and to collect dividends.
735265 Buy at the current price plus commission.
dfd1ad Closing a position. A gain is only real when you sell; until then it is "open profit".
4629e4 Sell your shares at the current price.
c5fcb2 Borrowing shares and selling them in the hope they fall, to buy them back cheaper. The potential loss is unlimited if the price rises.
d98a9c You win if the stock falls. It requires margin and pays a borrowing cost.
7d1955 Buying back the shares you sold short to return them and close the bet.
eafe5a Closes your short position.
44cb0e Buys only if the price falls to your level (or sells only if it rises). You control the price, not the timing.
84cbeb Stays pending until the price reaches it.
016956 An automatic sale if the price falls to a certain level. It limits losses without you watching the screen.
c0e2bf Triggers on its own when the level is crossed.
eda590 Share price times the number of shares: what the market says the whole company is worth.
d6cf10 Size of the company.
29bbcd How many years of earnings you pay when you buy the stock. A P/E of 15 is typical; one of 40 means the market expects a lot of growth (or a bubble).
51198c Lower = cheaper relative to what it earns.
d0409a How much the stock moves relative to the market. Beta 1: same as the index; 2: double (more risk); 0.5: half (defensive).
3cd5b2 The stock's risk relative to its exchange.
0b00e1 The part of the profits a company distributes to its shareholders, usually every quarter or year.
628d79 You receive it in cash as long as you hold the stock.
0fbd20 The highest price of the last year. It shows whether a stock is near its extremes.
42dbf0 Price range reference.
74a594 The lowest price of the last year.
70500f How many shares change hands per day. More volume = easier to get in and out without moving the price (liquidity).
080e85 The stock's liquidity.
5b55c4 The average price at which you bought your shares, counting all your purchases.
e6bc56 Basis for calculating your gain.
fe550d What you would gain or lose if you sold today. It is not real until you sell.
2601f8 Difference between the current value and your cost.
dbfed5 Difference between what your position is worth and what it cost you.
b54f1d Green wins, red loses.
2e4d1f Money the broker lends you to invest more than you have. It multiplies gains and losses; if it falls a lot, you are asked for more money (margin call) or they sell for you.
7623c6 If your collateral drops too low, the game liquidates positions.
eda137 A company sells shares to the public for the first time to raise capital. The founders become paper millionaires, but they share control.
ee6e77 You can take your business public if it is large and profitable.
10e8ee Funds that copy an entire index with very low fees. For most savers they have returned more than picking stocks by hand, because they diversify and charge almost nothing.
cfff56 You buy an entire market at once.
57f5fe Basic goods bought in large quantities: oil, gold, copper, wheat. Their prices rise with global demand and with supply shocks (wars, droughts).
0af9f3 Buy and sell commodities; their prices affect producing countries and companies.
7189b6 Oil, gold, copper, lithium, grains... Their price is set by world supply and demand.
cc971a Trade commodities.
3f0397 Loans you make to a government or company in exchange for fixed interest. Safer than stocks; if rates rise, the price of existing bonds falls.
7996ef Buy government bonds; you collect coupons every year.
d01260 The bonds you hold, their rate (coupon) and maturity.
e4d2e1 You collect interest until they mature or you sell them.
db2d23 The currency market is the largest in the world: about 7.5 trillion dollars a day. The price of one currency against another changes with interest rates, inflation and capital flows.
17c775 Buy and sell foreign currencies; protect your money from devaluation or speculate.
0dbde4 Exchanging your currency for another. Saving in a strong currency protects against devaluation, but it has an exchange cost.
aeb81d Trade currencies with their bid-ask spread.
e896ab Each country's interest rates and its currencies. Money tends to go where it pays more with less risk (carry trade).
daca62 Overview of interest and exchange rates.
87670f Markets react to company results, economic data, central bank decisions and political events.
ad7689 Recent news that moved prices.
e75595 Exchanges broadcast prices on a running tape (ticker). Green is up, red is down.
ba53b9 Choose which market and time frame you see in the bar.

087d77 Banks take deposits and lend them out; they profit from the difference between what they charge and what they pay. There are credit unions, regional, national and international banks and systemic giants.
c06eea Open accounts, take out loans, invest in funds or start your own bank.
a82950 Bank deposits that pay interest. Small banks usually pay more but fail more often; deposit insurance covers up to a certain amount per bank.
89d855 Deposit and withdraw. Spread your money across banks so you don't exceed the insurance.
28d86c Loans with interest. The rate depends on your credit history, your income and your collateral. A good history unlocks cheaper loans.
a74774 Ask for a loan according to your ability to pay.
2e60f9 A professional manager invests the money of many people in exchange for a fee. There are stock, bond, mixed and hedge funds.
6ed91b Invest in funds with different risk and fees.
14ec15 Founding a bank takes a lot of capital and a license from the regulator. A bank lends several times its capital (leverage), so it can be very profitable or collapse in a run.
180410 Found and run your bank: set rates, capital and risk.
637dab A score (in many countries from 300 to 850) that measures how good a payer you are. Paying on time raises it; falling behind sinks it for years.
d6cb57 Determines how much you can borrow and at what rate.
8c5109 A public fund that returns your savings if your bank fails, up to a limit. It prevents bank runs.
a16daa Covers your deposits per bank up to the cap.
2d99d1 A country's set of banks, funds and regulators. If the banks fall, credit freezes and the economy goes into recession (2008).
526e28 Health of the country's banking system, banking crises and help from the IMF and the World Bank.
e8cfc2 How well capitalized and healthy the banks are. Below a certain level the risk of a banking crisis rises.
ccb952 If it drops a lot, a crisis can break out.
38a3d0 The International Monetary Fund lends to countries in crisis in exchange for conditions (austerity, reforms). It helps stabilize, but it is usually unpopular.
b10cc7 Money for the treasury in a crisis, with conditions.
9bf7b4 Cutting public spending to reduce the deficit and debt. It gives creditors confidence, but it can slow the economy and cause protests.
5e12ea Less spending, less approval, more confidence.
583b5a Income, expenses, savings, debts and taxes. The basic rule: spend less than you earn and invest the difference.
f8dc23 Your personal account statement.
1d9a01 People you hire to improve your life: trainer, nutritionist, lawyer, accountant, publicist, security. They cost money, but they save time and risk.
09ce11 Each service gives a yearly benefit (health, taxes, sentences, scandals, security).
329cd6 A business sells products or services; its profit is what remains after paying costs, payroll, rent, taxes and depreciation. Most new businesses close in their first years.
0eb753 Open, expand, hire, take on debt or sell your companies.
dd3f07 The report that shows whether a company makes or loses money: sales minus cost of sales = gross profit; minus operating expenses = operating profit; minus interest and taxes = net profit.
16f53b How much your company sold and earned this month and over the last 12.
86a4da What remains at the end, after all expenses and taxes. It is what belongs to the owners.
0b062c The company's bottom line.
4efe03 Net profit divided by sales. A supermarket earns 2–4%; a software company, 20–30%.
a1f27a What percentage of each sale is profit.
085f31 How much of your installed capacity you are using. Very low: fixed costs going to waste; close to 100%: it's time to expand.
390e7e If it is maxed out, open another branch.
c6164b Demand is how much the market wants to buy; capacity, how much you can produce.
1b2f66 If demand exceeds your capacity you are leaving money on the table.
575a9b The trust of customers and partners. It takes years to build and days to lose.
30bca0 Affects your company's sales.
3b1f0f Additional outlets or plants. Expanding increases sales, but also fixed costs and risk.
e4948f Each branch adds capacity.
61384d Payroll is usually the biggest expense of a service company. Too few employees limit service; too many eat up the profit.
ca6029 Adjust staff to demand.
5744cf Oil, gas, lithium, copper, rare earths, uranium... Whoever has them earns foreign currency and geopolitical power; depending on a single resource is risky (Dutch disease).
1ae644 Your country's resource output; you can nationalize or ban exports.
3a2e23 The countries that produce the most of each resource. Concentrating production in a few countries makes prices fragile.
10df95 Who dominates each resource.
547cb5 A document that decides who inherits your property. Without a will, the law divides the inheritance by kinship and conflicts can arise.
afd6b7 Choose your heir: you continue the game as that person.
ed55fa Raising a child costs time and money, and their education largely defines their opportunities.
419984 Your children can inherit and carry on your legacy.
779bd0 A stable relationship brings support, happiness and sometimes shared income. It takes time and care.
05f8d7 Spend time with them to keep the relationship going.
678769 Your family of origin influences your opportunities, education and health.
45715c You can spend time with them and inherit from them.
2f8db6 The generations of your family and their ties.
7eb753 Your entire dynasty.
c2f4d2 Home, cars, companies and other assets. Assets that generate income (rents, businesses, investments) build wealth; those that only cost money (luxury cars) consume it.
9531a3 Your properties and their value.
85d487 Migrating changes wages, cost of living, language and opportunities. Millions of people migrate every year looking for work or safety.
472a0e Move to another province or country.
7fce21 Long-term goals. Writing them down and measuring progress increases the chance of achieving them.
4bde81 Your goals and unlocked achievements.

96f035 The entertainment and sports industry follows a power law: a few concentrate most of the fame and money, and the vast majority live on modest incomes. Talent, consistency, network and luck all weigh together.
18993d Music, acting, football, boxing, MMA, content, modeling, comedy, writing, cooking and DJ. Each with fans by territory, team, contracts, scandals, awards and tournaments.
c51430 An artistic or sports career is built over years: first your province, then your country and, if all goes well, the world.
aa431e Full panel: fans, level, team, works, shows, contracts and awards.
f369de An audience is won from the inside out: the local scene, then national radio and media, and finally international platforms and tours. The internet speeds up the jump for creators and DJs.
31d6c4 Your fans in your province, your country and the world. Each level has a ceiling (its population) and without activity fans gradually forget you.
631acf Skill is built through deliberate practice: the first gains are fast and the last ones very slow. A good coach speeds up the process.
eb1ff1 It goes up with training; it determines the quality of your works and your sports results. Natural talent multiplies every training session.
42ea01 Part of skill comes from innate conditions (coordination, ear, memory, physique), but without practice talent isn't enough.
f32ee4 Multiplies what you gain from each training session (from ×0.7 to ×1.35). You discover it when you start.
32a3c0 A fighter's wins, losses and knockouts. An unbeaten record sells more tickets.
6f5273 Your fights won, lost and by knockout.
ce335f Stars live off several sources: sales, royalties, salary, purses, shows and sponsorships, minus commissions and costs.
a508ba Everything your fame career generated last year, before taxes.
9bcd55 How the public and brands perceive you. A scandal sinks it and social causes restore it.
43d9a0 With a low image there are no sponsorships or good offers, and scandals are more likely.

f77d20 A coach corrects mistakes you can't see. Quality vs. price: the free one at a community center teaches the basics; an elite one costs several salaries a year, but speeds things up a lot and reduces injuries.
b2caf5 Multiplies what you gain in each training session. Charged every month.
88c2e2 Gets contracts, roles and sponsorships in exchange for a commission (in the real industry, typically 10–20% of what you generate).
04ea69 More reach, more offers and more auditions won, in exchange for their commission on all your fame income.

b2ed54 A label, publisher, production company or promoter gives you an advance and its machinery (distribution, promotion) in exchange for part of your income. The advance is deducted from your future royalties.
01d5ca Multiplies your reach and your recurring income during the years of the contract. A scandal can terminate it.
13dfdf The more fans you have, the better the offers. A strong agent gets more and better ones.
c21435 They arrive every year if you are well known. Compare advance, royalties, length and reach.
b6aa6a The percentage you get every time your work is sold or played. In streamed music, fractions of a cent are paid per play.
66c4d2 More royalties = more recurring income.
c96bb6 Brands pay to associate their image with yours. For many athletes and creators it is their main income.
856d6b Once a year, if you have fame 35+ and a good image.
f2b7c1 Industry awards (inspired by the big music, film, literature, food and sports awards) multiply attention and contracts.
69b6c3 If you had high-quality works during the year, you can be nominated and win.
30ddbf In boxing and MMA the sanctioning bodies rank fighters; to fight for the title you must be among the top.
168f54 You climb by beating opponents; the top 3 can fight for the world title.
dc1861 Social media controversies, statements, cancellations or plagiarism. A good public relations team reduces the damage.
81186c They cost you fans, image and sometimes the contract.
beca3d Successful stars rarely work alone: trainer, agent, publicist, lawyer and accountant.
74a307 Hire a coach and an agent here; the publicist and the lawyer in Services.
b04d29 What you create: songs, roles, videos, books, menus, routines. Quality varies: not everything you make will be a hit.
4e125c Each work adds fans according to its quality; hits get shared much more.
dd7974 Concerts, performances, shows and tours. In today's music, tours bring in more money than sales.
e45a6f They need a minimum number of fans in each territory. They bring money and fans, but they are tiring.
9e82fa Clubs sign whoever performs. You start in amateur leagues and move up divisions with level and results.
160415 Every year higher-level teams can sign you or you can be dropped; you earn a salary, championships and national-team call-ups.
7d5c49 Fighters usually have 2 to 4 fights a year: each one requires a training camp and leaves after-effects.
9db012 Choose an opponent: an easy one (small purse, little ranking), one at your level or a better one (bigger purse and more places if you win). Your odds are shown.
fb9956 The media report at local, national and international scale. Comparing sources helps you avoid falling for disinformation.
9f78f2 A portal with what's happening in your province, your country and the world.
3cc049 Complete explanations of every system in the game.
d711b7 Read by topic or replay the guided tour.
1a895b Game preferences.
982115 Sound, newspaper, map effects, dialogue frequency, currency and help bubbles.
c9158d The starting data comes from public sources (World Bank, IMF, ILO, UN).
5bfbed List of sources used.
b2d47a A university degree usually raises lifetime income significantly, although it varies a lot by field and country.
a4ed82 Studying takes years and sometimes tuition; it opens jobs and careers.
35eda5 Salaried jobs. Pay depends on your training, the occupation and your region's economy; unemployment makes it harder to get hired.
3e6389 Choose a job according to your qualifications.
4b137e Politics, the military, business and government: promotion ladders that can take you to ruling a country.
324e42 Each rank requires years, influence and intelligence.
